verdict.rationale: Navan documents the building blocks of in-flow coding as its own features: receipt scanning for on-the-go expenses, connected corporate cards, custom-field management, and an API for updating card transactions and expenses. Spend can also be broken down by vendor and category, and Ava works on real-time spend data. Nothing explicitly shows that transactions are coded automatically at the point of purchase, so close-readiness is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic merchant/category/memo coding at transaction time, memo capture, receipt-to-transaction matching, an accounting-close or ERP sync workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
